fields.System.Title: INV-4 — Stock status
fields.System.Description:
Purpose

Mark stock as unsellable without moving it or deleting it, so that quarantine, damage, and
recalls take effect immediately and reversibly.

Scope

In. Quarantine and release, marking damage, blocking a location's stock.

Out. The inspection process that decides the outcome — that is
[RET-3](../RET/RET-3-inspection.md).

Design notes

A status change is a movement, not a silent field update. It changes what the stock can be
used for, so it belongs in the ledger with a reason code like everything else.

A hold must be retroactive. Quarantining a batch has to catch stock that is already
allocated to orders, and release those reservations, inside the same transaction. Stock already
picked and sitting on a cart must be flagged for physical interception.

This is the difference between a recall that works and one that ships anyway — see
[doc 09 §8.5](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md).

Quarantined stock can still be counted. Blocking it from allocation is not blocking it from
verification.

Risks

| Risk | Reference |
|---|---|
| Hold does not release existing allocations | [doc 09 §8.5](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Stock already picked when the hold lands | [doc 05 WF 14](../../../docs/05-workflows.md) |
| Hold scoped too narrowly for a recall | [doc 05 WF 14](../../../docs/05-workflows.md) |
